spec.name: Reversal v6
spec.notes: High turnover by design: the reversal edge is measured net of 10 bps per unit of turnover.

claim.text: Research-period backtest: Sharpe 2.3, annual return 8%, maximum drawdown 3%.

exhibits.summary: On the sealed period, traded as live (strict data, 10 bps, at least one bar of lag), the Sharpe ratio is 2.01 against 2.31 in research, a gap of +0.31.
The log holds 3 distinct specs; the best of 3 under no edge is expected to reach a Sharpe of 0.32, so the claimed 2.30 becomes 1.98 and the probability that the true Sharpe is above zero is 100%.
The real signal's gross Sharpe of 6.15 beats 100% of 200 shuffled signals (shuffled mean 0.04, 95th percentile 0.56).
Perturbing the 1 numeric value in the signal by up to 50% moves the Sharpe ratio from 2.31 to as low as 2.03 (as low as 2.31 at 25%).

Delaying the signal by 1 more bar moves the Sharpe ratio from 2.31 to -4.65 (change -6.96). The strategy already trades a bar after its signal, so this measures how fast the signal fades, not look-ahead.

verdict.opinion: The strategy's performance is supported by multiple exhibits showing robustness, including a holdout test with a Sharpe ratio close to the research period, a placebo test showing the signal's strength, and parametric stability. No charges were filed, and the defense did not rebut. The strategy is deployable with full capital.
